AReading: Data Centre Safety Briefing
Read the memo from the facilities manager, then choose the correct answer for each question.

To: All new IT trainees  ·  Subject: Data centre visit — Friday

Before your first visit to our data centre on Friday, please read the following safety information carefully. All visitors must sign in at reception and complete a short safety briefing before entering the server room. Inside, you must wear an ESD wrist strap whenever you handle components — even a small electrostatic discharge can destroy a memory module.

Please watch out for trip hazards. Although our cable management is generally good, some floor panels were removed last week for maintenance and the area is marked with yellow tape. Do not step over open panels; walk around them. The room is loud (around 80 dB) because of the ventilation system, so ear protection is recommended for stays of more than one hour. Finally, food and drink are strictly forbidden — liquids and electronics are a dangerous combination. A full risk assessment is attached to this memo. — M. Weber, Facilities Manager

CGrammar: Modal Verbs for Rules and Advice
Choose the modal verb that fits each safety rule. Think about whether it is an obligation, a prohibition or a recommendation.
1. You wear an ESD strap when handling RAM — it is a strict rule.
2. You eat or drink in the server room — it is forbidden.
3. Employees report all accidents to their supervisor; it is required by law.
4. You take regular screen breaks — it is good for your eyes.
5. Visitors wear a helmet in this area; it is optional but recommended.
6. You be certified to repair high-voltage equipment — untrained staff are not allowed.
7. Trainees lift heavy servers alone; always ask a colleague for help.
